description: Second-order taint corpus: multi-file flows where untrusted data is WRITTEN to a persistence layer in one place and READ BACK somewhere else, with no call edge joining the writer to the reader. Each case is a self-contained mini-application in its own directory and is scanned as its own project root, preserving case isolation for resource-scoped vector channels (with receiver fallback) and the ORM channel's unresolved bare-class-name fallback.
why: Opengrep PR #779 (https://github.com/opengrep/opengrep/pull/779) adds interfile taint analysis, but its design keys every taint signature to a CALL EDGE. A second-order flow has no call edge between writer and reader, so that architecture structurally cannot express these flows regardless of how the rules are written. Rowan models them as persistence CHANNELS instead (rowan/passes/cross_file.py: _collect_orm_write_channels / _expr_reads_orm_channel / _function_reads_orm_channel for ORM, _collect_vector_write_channels / _function_reads_vector_channel for vector stores). This corpus measures the size of that gap and, just as importantly, the size of Rowan's own remaining gap: five of the channels listed as #156 follow-ups in cross_file.py are not modeled at all yet.

scoring.hit: a CF-SINK-001 or CF-RETURN-001 finding anchored in the case's `reader_file`. Cross-file findings anchor on the CALLER -- the reader function -- which is the entry point of the second-order half of the flow.
scoring.expected_detect: gates: every one of these must be a hit.
scoring.expected_known_gap: reported, never gated. These are the roadmap. A gap that starts producing a hit is printed as GAP CLOSED and should be promoted to expected=detect.
scoring.expected_clean: gates: no cross-file finding may anchor in `reader_file`.
scoring.expected_known_fp: reported, never gated. A negative Rowan currently gets wrong; printed as FP FIXED once it stops firing.

notes.boundary_proxy: queue_celery_archive_path is credited as a hit, but NOT because Rowan connected the send_task() payload to the worker -- it does not model the queue channel at all. `_collect_task_queue_nodes` marks every @shared_task function as a structural trust boundary, so its parameters are treated as untrusted whether or not anything untrusted is actually enqueued. That reaches the right conclusion here without pairing a writer to a reader, so the case carries `detection: "boundary_proxy"` and is excluded from the paired-channel count.
notes.arg_binding: rag_loop_rebind_ssrf and the two detected RAG cases differ only in how the retrieved value reaches the sink call. `_vector_read_vars` records the variable the retrieval was ASSIGNED to; `_arg_expr_is_caller_tainted` then needs that variable to appear in the argument expression. `run_subquery(matches[0].metadata["sql"])` names `matches` and binds; `for hit in hits: fetch_page(hit.metadata["origin_url"])` rebinds through the loop variable and does not. Same for the ORM channel via `_orm_classes_by_var`.
notes.sanitizers: neg_sanitized_before_write is the regression control for a sink-specific transformation before persistence. Its allowlist (`^[a-z0-9_-]{1,64}$`) rejects invalid application identifiers, then `shlex.quote` materializes shell safety into the exact value written to the ORM. The channel collector follows that transformed value without globally treating a regex as safe for unrelated sinks such as SSRF.
notes.chroma_fixture: rag_chroma_source_path uses the LangChain Chroma wrapper for both add_documents and similarity_search. The writer calls its wrapper `collection` and the reader calls its wrapper `vector_store`; Rowan pairs them by the literal persistent-client path and collection name, not coincidental local receiver spelling. The earlier fixture mixed native chromadb.Collection (whose insertion API is add) with LangChain's add_documents API.
notes.non_crossfile_findings: Several cases also produce ordinary single-file findings (NS-CMDI-002 on the sink helper, TNT-STORED-001 on the writer, ns-aiml-052 on the RAG reader). Those are not second-order detections -- none of them joins the writer to the reader -- so the scorer ignores every rule id except the CF-* family.

cases.description: A subscriber registers a callback URL. A scheduler process reads the row back and POSTs to it, giving SSRF against internal endpoints. Writer and reader share only the webhooks table.
The user names their own export file. A systemd-run worker polls the job table and interpolates the stored name into a soffice command line.
Tenants author notification templates. A Celery task loads the stored body and renders it through a non-sandboxed Jinja environment.

Index poisoning into path traversal. The uploader controls the `source` label stored as chunk metadata; the answering path resolves that label back to a file on disk to attach the original as a citation.

Analysts publish SQL snippets into a shared FAISS index. The assistant retrieves the nearest snippet for a question and wraps it into a preview query, so whoever published the snippet controls the SQL a different user runs.

cases.sink: exports/packaging.py:package_directory (tarfile.add + shutil.rmtree under a base directory)
cases.description: The request handler dispatches by task NAME over the broker, so nothing imports the worker and no call edge exists. Rowan reaches the right conclusion through the @shared_task boundary heuristic rather than by pairing the payload to the parameter -- see notes.boundary_proxy.

cases.gap: argument binding is lost when the retrieved value reaches the sink through a `for` loop variable instead of the variable the retrieval was assigned to (notes.arg_binding).
cases.description: Bookmark metadata carries a submitter-controlled origin URL. The freshness checker retrieves matching bookmarks and re-fetches each URL in a loop, which is SSRF. The channel arms and the reader is recognized as a vector read, but the sink argument is `hit.metadata[...]`, not `hits`, so no cross-file finding is emitted.

cases.gap: no cache channel. cross_file.py models ORM and vector-store persistence only; a Redis set/get pair is invisible to it.
cases.description: A user's mail signature is cached on write so the digest mailer never hits the database. The mailer renders the cached markup through Jinja to expand merge fields.

cases.gap: no blob-storage channel. `s3.put_object` / `s3.get_object` are not recognized as a write/read pair, and the receiver name `s3` does not match the vector-store receiver hint.
cases.description: The upload endpoint stores the manifest verbatim in S3 and returns immediately. The import worker pulls the object back and deserializes it with the unsafe YAML loader.

cases.gap: no file-write/file-read channel (listed as a #156 follow-up in cross_file.py's module comment).
cases.description: Host provisioning requests are appended to a JSON state file. A timer-driven reconciler reads the file and interpolates the requested hostname into an nmcli command line.

cases.gap: no agent-memory channel. `memory.save_context` / `memory.load_memory_variables` are not recognized, and `memory` does not match the vector-store receiver hint.
cases.description: Every user turn is written to the conversation buffer. On a later request the planner replays the buffer, extracts the last fenced Python block and executes it, so a user can plant the code the agent runs.

Byte-for-byte the same model, read idiom and cross-file sink as orm_flask_webhook_ssrf, except the only writer is a bootstrap routine that fills target_url from deployment config. Nothing untrusted reaches the field, so the channel must not arm.

Exercises _channel_matches. Two unrelated Django apps in one repo each define a model class called Invoice with a `notes` field. billing's handler writes a request value to billing.Invoice.notes; support's exporter reads support.Invoice.notes into a shell command. The tainted write must not arm the reader of the other class.

Field-level scoping. The handler writes an untrusted value to PartnerHook.display_label; target_url comes from config. The dispatcher reads target_url and secret only, never display_label, so the armed channel and the read are on different fields of the same model.

The archive name is checked against ^[a-z0-9_-]{1,64}$ with fullmatch and rejected with a 400 before it is ever persisted, so the value the worker shells out with is safe by construction. Rowan arms the channel anyway because the written value traces back to request.POST -- see notes.sanitizers.
